solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone hunts around for a band to play at their dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small group of musicians, typically a jazz or dance outfit.

clue.text: Usyk say needs minute stopping man

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other like a cork

blocks.note: a chap is a man
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A boxer like Usyk needs only a minute to stop his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Oleksandr Usyk is a Ukrainian heavyweight boxing world champion; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Usyk holds world heavyweight titles, so he is an instance of a title holder, informally a champ.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of girl's word is dropped

blocks.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
someone abducted has been taken

explanation.surface: Reports that a girl had almost been abducted turn out to be false.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken and wrong are adjective synonyms for being in error or incorrect.

indicators.note: something that has collapsed falls into a heap, its parts in disorder

blocks.note: the island's name taken as letters

explanation.surface: A lively ruler in Borneo has fallen from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spritely' looks like a misspelling of sprightly, meaning lively, but here it means of the sprites.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, ruling over sprites like Puck.

clue.text: Great many supporting Labour up in vote

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top
in a down clue, supporting puts one piece underneath the other

blocks.note: Lab is the short form of the Labour Party
a lot is a great many

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people back Labour at the election.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a vote, especially a secret one held in writing.

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: your kin are your relatives
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Family members are fitting a big new oven in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a furnace or oven for firing pottery, bricks or drying hops.

clue.text: Two for one for example in Bury

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for bury

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A two-for-one offer, for example, in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two for one' reads like a shop deal, but it means 'two, for one', a single instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a whole number, so it serves as one example of the class of whole numbers.

clue.text: Pub to ban Scotsman, wild sort

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
to bar someone is to ban them
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A pub decides to ban a Scotsman who has been behaving wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is an uncivilised, savage or brutish person, a wild type.

clue.text: At fault, not entirely sober, Pilsner drunk

indicators.note: not entirely means the word lacks part of itself, here its final letter
a drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its last letter
the lager's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who was not quite sober after drinking Pilsner is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Being responsible for a mishap means being the one to blame or culpable for it.

blocks.note: taken as written
a key, or cay, is a low island, so an isle

explanation.surface: An important passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A key passage' sounds like a crucial piece of writing; key is the Florida Keys sense of a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, a passage through them.

clue.text: Peace as interrupted by the French

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

blocks.note: as and since both mean because
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Calm has been disturbed by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace and quiet; silence is the absence of noise, tranquillity in that sense.

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled together, so the letters of the fabulist's name are rearranged

blocks.note: the Greek fable-teller's name taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Aesop has stirred together a vegetable soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed up' looks like one phrase, but only 'mixed' does the work; 'up' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a thick soup made from dried peas, a broth of vegetables.

indicators.note: something agitated is shaken up, so its letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worked-up sceptic keeps interrupting.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to impose yourself unwelcomely, intrude or interfere uninvited.

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to ruin something horribly in the last round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means last in a series, coming at the very end.

clue.text: Fertiliser in firm mass on display

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places one piece directly above the next

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the symbol for mass in physics
to post a notice is to put it up on display

explanation.surface: A company shows off a large heap of fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Compost is decayed organic matter dug into soil to enrich it, a natural plant food.

clue.text: Old writer in problem about anthology

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for problem is read backwards
in places the writer's piece inside the turned word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a sum is an arithmetic problem
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A veteran author has trouble with a collection of writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author, but in crosswords it is often the pointed tip of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a volume gathering several works, often by one author, so a collection.

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so this is a word picked up by ear

blocks.note: Ringo Starr was the drummer in the Beatles, so he is one of them

explanation.surface: Was it an insect, or perhaps Ringo Starr, who got caught?
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles' name was itself a pun on the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases, of the order Coleoptera.

blocks.note: f. abbreviates following, as in page references
taken as written
the rage, as in all the rage, is the current trend

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician who jumps on whatever is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage leads the UK's Reform party and is MP for Clacton.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Farage is a British populist politician who sits in Parliament for Reform UK.

clue.text: Picture one GI covered in hair

indicators.note: something covered in another thing has that thing all around it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mane is a long head of hair
taken as written; a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Visualise a single American soldier covered in hair.
explanation.walkthrough: GI, an American soldier, is used as written rather than turned into anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, to visualise it.

clue.text: Virtuoso lacking piano to bring into use

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is taken away

blocks.note: a virtuoso is a skilled expert
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A virtuoso without a piano still has to put their skills to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or influence is to apply it, putting it to work.

indicators.note: something encased in another is wrapped by it on both sides

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means different

explanation.surface: A plant unlike others has been sealed in lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is any leafy plant grown for cooking, such as parsley or spinach.

indicators.note: something told is spoken out, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A dog features in a story someone has narrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun but is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, exactly what a detective does when shadowing a suspect.

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a few Canada geese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, as is an adage.

clue.text: Film director in story by composer

blocks.note: a spiel is a glib story or patter
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A film director appears in a tale told alongside a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg is the American film-maker behind Jaws and E.T.

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of Personage
a vent is an opening, as for air or smoke

explanation.surface: A celebrity is at last opening the exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occasion or organised happening, such as a show or exhibition.
